Daily Criminal Report No. 140
628
Complt:- Bernard Lilienstern, 32, German Jewish
refugee, m/factory owner, 1143/106 East
Yuhang Road, Pass No. 7197.
22-12-44
Places:- On the first floor front room of a Chinese
style dwelling house situated at above address.
Time reported:- at 8 p.m. 13.12.44.
Time of Murder etc:- At about 7 p.m. 13.12.44.
Property stolen:- One silver pocket watch with yellow
coloured dial. $4800.00
$200 in notes. 200.00
Value $5000.00
Victim murdered:- Hermann Lilienstern, 64, German Jewish
refugee, m/factory owner, 1143/106 East
Yuhang Road, Pass No. 7197.
Death Certificate states:-
1. "Lilienstern Factories" Dr. Braun.
2. "on arrival" General Hospital.
Victim assaulted:- Complainant.
Doctors certificate states:-
"Laceration on the rear part
of left ear"
Sigh. Dr. Liao Yoong Long
Police Hosp.
Inquiries by D.S.I. Yen Yoong, C.D.C.1030 and
Yang Hui Ling
the undersigned.
At 8 p.m. 13.12.44 a telephone message was received from
Mr. Rachtel, 8b Wayside Rd to the effect that there was a
foreigner lying dead at 1143/106 East Yuhang Rd.
The above mentioned detectives proceeded to the afore-
mentioned place and after preliminary enquiries the following
was ascertained.
At about 7 p.m. 13.12.44 four male Chinese, one armed with
a dagger and another with a piece of rope entered the complts
room via the unlocked rear and room doors and after attacking the
complt with a dagger and the complts father with clenched fists
resulting in the complt receiving injuries to his ear whilst
his father died immediately from the effect of the attack.
The robbers remained on the premises for about 10 minutes
and then decamped taking with them $200 in notes and the complts
pocket watch. No. No.
The body of the murdered person was taken to the General
Hospital and after being certified dead was removed to the Public
Mortuary pending inquest.

-2-

Further enquiries revealed the following.

The scene of the murder is a Chinese style dwelling house
situated at 1143/106 J. Yuhang Rd. The whole house is occupied
by the complt and his father and mother named Herman and Anna
respectively. The ground floor of the house is used by the
complt as a Cron and Nickel Plating Factory, whilst the complt
and his family reside on the first floor. The first floor is
divided into two rooms, the front room being used by them as
a living room whilst the rear room is utilised as a kitchen.

Between the hours of 7 a.m. and 5 p.m. daily the rear door
of the house is always left unlocked by the complt.

At about 7 p.m. 13.12.44 whilst the complt's mother was
cooking in the kitchen she heard steps outside in the corridor
and on going out to investigate she saw standing next to the
kitchen door four male Chinese whose description she does not
know due to the fact that she is very short sighted. One of the
male Chinese then informed her that they were the Police they
searched her but found nothing of any value on her person.
They then led her into the living room where the complt and
his father were eating.

The following are the description of the four robbers:-

1. Male Chinese, age about 35, height about 5'3"
slim built, long thin face, wearing a Chinese
long grey gown and grey felt hat.

2. Male Chinese, age about 30, height about 5'6",
slim built, round face, wearing a Chinese long
grey gown with grey felt hat.
IN POSSESSION OF A ROPE 1½ yards long.

3. Description unavailable.

4. " " "

On the above described male Chinese together with the
complt's mother entering the living room, the first described
robber who was in possession of a dagger immediately attacked
the complt injuring his head and at the same time the 2nd
described robber attempted to tie the rope round the complt's
neck. At this instance the complt's father (the injured person)
came to the assistance of the complt, resulting in the 2nd

-3-
described a robber with his clenched fists striking the complt's
father on the chest, resulting in him collapsing onto the room
floor where he died.

During the above mentioned occurrence the 3rd and 4th
described robbers were standing on guard at the room door.
On seeing their victim falling onto the floor the 1st and 2nd
described robbers commenced to search the pockets of the complt
and his father and on finding nothing they warned the inmates by signs
not to raise an alarm and left via point of entry after re-
maining on the premises for about 15 minutes.

After an elapse of about 5 minutes the 3rd described robber
returned alone to the living room/and again searched the complt
and took from him his pocket watch and $200 in notes, and left
immediately.

At about 7.45 p.m. 13.12.44 on seeing that the robbers
did not return again the complt immediately telephoned to
Dr. Herbert Gruenberger residing at 305/58 Kungping Road to
attend to his father. The above mentioned doctor on arriving
and examining him pronounced the victim dead and issued the
following Death Certificate:-
Name: Hermann Lilienstern.
Address: 1143/106 E. Yuhang Rd.
Primary: Heartemboly.
Secondary: Angina Pectoris.
Died: 13.12.44.

By this time a friend of the complt named Hans Loewensohn
Tongshan Road
residing at 725/65 came to visit the complt and on him being
told what had occurred he immediately relayed the information
to Dr. Mantel who in turn informed the station as described
above.

The Pao Chia member on duty at the entrance of lane 1143
E. Yuhang Rd between the hours of 4 p.m. and 8 p.m. 13.12.44
named:-
Zhu Tao Ying, ( 曾道瀛 ), 13, Kompo,
a/u apprentice, 1143/89 E. Yuhang Rd;
was located and on being questioned stated that during his
tour of duty did not hear or see anything unusual.

The complt on being further questioned stated that
on the 24.11.44 the power in his factory was cut off by the

-4-

Shanghai Power Co., resulting in him on the spot giving
notice of dismissal to his Chinese foreman and four Chinese
employees. The four employees then demanded $30,000 each
as compensation which the culprit refused and a quarrel starting
which nearly ending in a fight. This quarrel was eventually
settled by the culprit through the medium of his foreman and it
was agreed that he would pay each employee $12,000 compensation.
The culprit also paid his foreman $2,000 compensation.

The culprit on being asked for the names and addresses
of his former employees stated that he had no record of same
as all Chinese employed in his factory were hired by his foreman,
named Lew Sung Chang (劉松昌), having no residence in Shanghai,
who had on loosing his job returned to Sushih.

All endeavours are at present being made by detectives
to discover a clue that might lead to the apprehension of the
persons responsible of the crime.

F.P. Bureau notified and on attending took photographs.
Due to the fact that all places likely to retain latent
fingerprints have already been handled by the inmates no finger-
prints could be found.

Enquiries proceeding.

Circulated.

All concerned notified.

（印：雷古默凡）
J. I. Kramer.

Senior Detective 1/c.
